narrative:
The tide is out, and the harbour smells of salt and wet stone. You stand on the crown of the wall at first light with your palm flat against the coping. It's the habit of years. You're listening for a fault, though stone doesn't speak. It only gives you cold, and a roughness that you know better than your own knuckles.

You laid every course of it. You remember the summer the quarry carts came down the hill in a line, and the winter you spent wedging blocks into the swell with your hands split open. Now the wall curls around the water like an arm around a sleeping child. Fishing boats rock behind it, and the masts knock together softly. Beyond it the open sea heaves grey and restless, and the breakers spend themselves against your work and fall back.

*Hold,* you think, the way you do each morning. *Hold one more day.*

You kneel where the mortar is darker than it should be. A seam has opened, no wider than a blade, near the seaward face. Your thumbnail finds it, and a trickle of grit runs out. It's too small to frighten anyone and too new to ignore. You've seen how great ruin begins with something just this size.

"You'll wear a hole in it, staring like that."

The voice comes from the stair at the landward end. A figure climbs into the pale light, a spear on his shoulder and a salt-stiffened cloak pulled tight. It's the guard. He has your name, as the merchant at the sail-loft has your name, and the whole waterfront has long since given up being confused. Children call you **Ajax Stone**. They call him **Ajax Spear**. The sail-seller they call **Ajax Cloth**, and he answers to it happily enough.

"Morning, Spear," you say, without rising.

"Is that a crack?" He walks over and lowers himself beside you with a grunt, his knees popping. He has stood on this wall through a hundred nights, and he is more at ease here than he ever is in a tavern. "I walked the whole length at the change of watch and saw nothing."

"You wouldn't. You look for men, not for stone." You press the seam again, and more grit gives way. "Here. Feel."

He lays two gloved fingers against it and frowns. The easy humour drains out of his face. "The storm last week?"

"Maybe. Or the footing is moving underneath, and then it's no storm at all." You say it flatly, because you don't wish to say it at all. A wall that settles can be mended. A wall that is being undermined by the sea is a longer and uglier story.

Spear is quiet for a moment. Out past the mouth of the harbour a gull cries, and the first boats are stirring, with the scrape of oars and the call of men hauling nets aboard. Somewhere in the lanes behind you a shutter bangs open. The town is waking up, and it has no idea what you've just put your thumb on.

"Who else knows?" he asks.

"You do."

"Then I'd keep it that way until you're sure." He meets your eye. "Folk here sleep because of this wall, Ajax. Tell them it's cracking, and they'll stop trusting it before you've found out whether you should."

You look down at the seam, then out along the grey curve of the stonework, and then at the water. The tide has turned. You can hear it, a low hush against the base of the wall, patient and unhurried, as it has always been.

quick_actions.text: Mark the seam with chalk and quietly keep watch on it
Climb down the seaward face at low tide to inspect the footing
Ask Spear what he has noticed on his night watches

scene_description: Dawn on a grey stone harbour wall curving around a sheltered bay. Two weathered men in rough cloaks kneel on the wall's top: a broad-shouldered mason with split, stone-dusty hands pressing a thumb to a narrow dark crack in the mortar, and a guard with a spear over his shoulder and salt-stiffened cloak looking on with a worried frown. Fishing boats with tall masts rock behind the wall, open grey sea and breakers beyond, pale morning light, gulls overhead.

summary_update.world: A sheltered harbour town, protected by a great curved seawall. Locals distinguish the three men named Ajax by nicknames: Ajax Stone (the mason), Ajax Spear (the guard) and Ajax Cloth (the sail merchant).
summary_update.current_situation: At dawn on the harbour wall, Ajax the mason has found a new seam opening in the seaward mortar. Ajax-2 the guard has seen it too and advises keeping it secret until the cause is known.
new_major_events: Ajax the mason discovers a fresh crack in the seaward face of the harbour wall; the guard Ajax agrees to keep it quiet for now.
upcoming_events: Determine whether the crack is storm damage or the sea undermining the wall's footing
Decide whether and when to tell the townsfolk

character_updates.current_state: Kneeling on the crown of the wall at dawn, worried by a new hairline crack in the seaward mortar. Intends to find out whether the footing is failing. Known as Ajax Stone.
character_updates.relationships: Friend of the guard Ajax (Spear); shares his name with him and with the sail merchant Ajax (Cloth).

character_updates.name: Ajax
character_updates.current_state: Has just climbed the wall after the night watch, examined the crack and urged the mason to stay quiet until sure. Known as Ajax Spear. Tired, grim, protective of the town's confidence.
character_updates.relationships: Old friend of the mason; trusts his judgement about the wall.
